newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - April 25.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. FRATERNITE MATIN - Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan leads development talks in western Ivory Coast; talks focus on decentralisation of economic planning and a Canadian-led nickel mine project, gold exploration, infrastructure improvements, mechanisation of farming, and livestock and soja farming. - Unilever's Ivorian subsidiary Blohorn advertises 14.5 pct year-on half-year turnover rise to 44.39 billion CFA francs for 1996/97 (Oct 1-March 31) against 36.76 billion in 1995/96. - Economist and author of "The Price of CFA Money: Pros and Cons for the Franc Zone", Olivier Vallee, says convertibility of currency between African states should be resolved before they take a view on adopting an African currency against Europe's proposed Euro. LE JOUR - Minister for Planning and Development Ahoua N'Doli calls for dissemination of information on West African Economic and Monetary Union to help Ivorian businesses compete. - University research group for promoting ideas of President Henri Konan Bedie holds seminar on "Modernisation and Development of Ivory Coast". - Move to restrict top speeds of public transport vehicles draws fire from transport operators; some threaten lightning strikes; union urges talks. LA VOIE - International talks on decentralisation of political power by governments opens at Ivory Coast's national asssembly with delegates attending from French and main Ivorian parties. - Accounting systems for West African economic and monetary union come into effect from January 1, 1998, says Dakar-based West African Central Bank President Charles Konan Banny.
